decisions.quote: In summary, econometric evidence to support the hypothesis that changes in the payroll weight affected the distribution of manufacturing employment among US states in the 1978 to 1994 period appears less strong than G&M asserted even when using G&M’s data and methods.
decisions.reason: The study primarily re-analyses Goolsbee and Maydew's 1978–1994 dataset and methods (checking sample construction, numerical reproducibility, and specification/clustering robustness) before adding a newer-data extension, which qualifies it as a reproduction.

decisions.quote: I identify an apparent but inconsequential error in G&M’s sample, and I replicate the most widely cited result in the original article. Other results are substantively but not quantitatively replicated. I show that G&M’s results are sensitive to relatively arbitrary choices about the sample that is used.
decisions.reason: Re-running the original analysis reproduced the most widely cited result but yielded quantitative discrepancies on other results (computational issues), and the main finding was sensitive to sample choices, preferred specifications, and state-clustered standard errors (robustness challenges).
